\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{উদ্বেগ} (udbeg)}{উদ্বেগ (udbeg)}]{\bn{উদ্বেগ} (udbeg) — anxiety; unease}

\label{lesson:BN-C442-udbeg}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to get flustered, then the Bengali for to pound.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{উদ্বেগ}}
\textbf{\bn{উদ্বেগ}} — \emph{udbeg} — \textquotedblleft{}anxiety; unease\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ছেলের} \bn{জ্বর} \bn{নিয়ে} \bn{বাবার} \bn{উদ্বেগ} \bn{বাড়ল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{chheler jbôr niye bābār udbeg bāṛlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Father's anxiety over his son's fever grew.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{উদ্বেগ}} (\emph{udbeg}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{udvega}, \textquotedblleft{}trembling, agitation, distress\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{udbeg}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{udbeg}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chheler jbôr niye bābār udbeg bāṛlô.} — Father's anxiety over his son's fever grew.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to get flustered, then the Bengali for to pound, then say \emph{udbeg} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{উদ্বেগ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Anxiety; unease\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{দুর্ভাবনা} (durbhābônā)}{দুর্ভাবনা (durbhābônā)}]{\bn{দুর্ভাবনা} (durbhābônā) — anxious thoughts; worry}

\label{lesson:BN-C442-durbhabona}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to pound, then the Bengali for anxiety.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{দুর্ভাবনা}}
\textbf{\bn{দুর্ভাবনা}} — \emph{durbhābônā} — \textquotedblleft{}anxious thoughts; worry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{রাতে} \bn{দুর্ভাবনায়} \bn{আমি} \bn{জেগে} \bn{ছিলাম।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rāte durbhābônāy āmi jege chhilām.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I lay awake at night with worry.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{দুর্ভাবনা}} (\emph{durbhābônā}) is Sanskrit \emph{durbhāvanā}, \textquotedblleft{}a bad thought\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), \emph{dur-} \textquotedblleft{}ill\textquotedblright{} on \emph{bhāvanā} \textquotedblleft{}reflection\textquotedblright{}; Bengali uses it for anxious thoughts. \bn{ভাবা} (taught), to think, is the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{durbhābônā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{durbhābônā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rāte durbhābônāy āmi jege chhilām.} — I lay awake at night with worry.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to pound, then the Bengali for anxiety, then say \emph{durbhābônā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{দুর্ভাবনা} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Anxious thoughts; worry\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{অস্থির} (ôsthir)}{অস্থির (ôsthir)}]{\bn{অস্থির} (ôsthir) — restless; unsettled}

\label{lesson:BN-C442-osthir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for anxiety, then the Bengali for anxious thoughts.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{অস্থির}}
\textbf{\bn{অস্থির}} — \emph{ôsthir} — \textquotedblleft{}restless; unsettled\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{সারাদিন} \bn{ফোন} \bn{না} \bn{পেয়ে} \bn{মীরা} \bn{অস্থির} \bn{হল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sārādin phon nā peye mīrā ôsthir hôlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Mira grew restless after a whole day without a call.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{অস্থির}} (\emph{ôsthir}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{asthira}, \textquotedblleft{}unsteady, shaking\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams): \emph{a-} \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{} on \emph{sthira} \textquotedblleft{}firm\textquotedblright{}, the \bn{স্থির} of \bn{স্থির} \bn{করা} (taught), to decide.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôsthir}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ôsthir}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sārādin phon nā peye mīrā ôsthir hôlô.} — Mira grew restless after a whole day without a call.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for anxiety, then the Bengali for anxious thoughts, then say \emph{ôsthir} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{অস্থির} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Restless; unsettled\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{নিশ্চিন্ত} (nishchintô)}{নিশ্চিন্ত (nishchintô)}]{\bn{নিশ্চিন্ত} (nishchintô) — free of worry; at ease}

\label{lesson:BN-C442-nishchinto}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for anxious thoughts, then the Bengali for restless.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{নিশ্চিন্ত}}
\textbf{\bn{নিশ্চিন্ত}} — \emph{nishchintô} — \textquotedblleft{}free of worry; at ease\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ফলাফল} \bn{দেখে} \bn{বাবা} \bn{নিশ্চিন্ত} \bn{হলেন।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{phôlāphôl dekhe bābā nishchintô hôlen.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Seeing the result, my father stopped worrying.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{নিশ্চিন্ত}} (\emph{nishchintô}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{niścinta}, \textquotedblleft{}unconcerned, careless\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams): \emph{niḥ-} \textquotedblleft{}without\textquotedblright{} on \emph{cintā}, the \bn{চিন্তা} (taught) that means both a thought and a worry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nishchintô}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nishchintô}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phôlāphôl dekhe bābā nishchintô hôlen.} — Seeing the result, my father stopped worrying.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for anxious thoughts, then the Bengali for restless, then say \emph{nishchintô} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{নিশ্চিন্ত} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Free of worry; at ease\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ছটফট} \bn{করা} (chhôṭphôṭ kôrā)}{ছটফট করা (chhôṭphôṭ kôrā)}]{\bn{ছটফট} \bn{করা} (chhôṭphôṭ kôrā) — to fidget; to toss and turn}

\label{lesson:BN-C442-chhotphot-kora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for restless, then the Bengali for free of worry.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ছটফট} \bn{করা}}
\textbf{\bn{ছটফট} \bn{করা}} — \emph{chhôṭphôṭ kôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to fidget; to toss and turn\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{জ্বরে} \bn{ছেলেটা} \bn{সারারাত} \bn{ছটফট} \bn{করল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jbôre chheleṭā sārārāt chhôṭphôṭ kôrlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The boy tossed and turned all night with fever.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{তিনি} \bn{ব্যথায়} \bn{ছটফট} \bn{করলেন}, \emph{tini bæthāy chhôṭphôṭ kôrlen}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ছটফট} \bn{করা}} (\emph{chhôṭphôṭ kôrā}) is \emph{chhôṭphôṭ}, an expressive word that paints quick, restless movement, with \emph{kôrā}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2814).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chhôṭphôṭ kôrā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jbôre chheleṭā sārārāt chhôṭphôṭ kôrlô.} — The boy tossed and turned all night with fever.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for restless, then the Bengali for free of worry, then say \emph{chhôṭphôṭ kôrā} again
\end{itemize}
